Definition: middle voice from a compound of G1722 and G3775; to take in one's ear, i.e. to listen:--hearken.
BiblicalUsage: Peter stands up with the eleven on the day of Pentecost and says, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words, in Acts 2:14 — the word is an ear opened wide to listen.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Pentecost began with listening, and the gospel still begins the same way — hearken first, and the Spirit does the rest.
RelatedTopics: Outpouring of the Spirit; Listening Well
